title: Very unfriendly to people with disabilities
body:
I have been a subscriber for five years. Bugs that I reported three years ago still have not been fixed every week. I report a bug. They never fix them. 

For instance, you have 12 minutes left, you win another 15 min, instead of telling you that you have 27 minutes, it will say you have 21 minutes, then on the next screen it will say that you have 36 minutes. 

How can an app be so broken?
Because millions of people pay for this app, but they don’t care and they don’t put any money into improving it

The user interface needs an overhaul. So much blank space to be used and yet on many exercises the font size is smaller than 4 point, which is ridiculous for older users and those who are visually impaired.

Also, as someone who has Parkinson’s, too much emphasis is put on speed over accuracy with timed exercises which are impossible for me to attempt.

title: App has gone downhill, don’t pay for subscription.
body:
Duolingo is slowly turning into a money-making machine, and it’s becoming obvious when you read the other negative reviews.

I bought Duolingo Max Annual thinking I’d actually use it to learn French. Instead, after just two months, my daily time on the app had dropped to around 11 seconds a day - enough to complete the shortest possible lesson.

At this point, Duolingo feels less like a language-learning app and more like a game with cute sound effects, animations and a plush green owl. The problem is, I didn’t pay for Duolingo to play a game. I paid to learn French.

The constant “motivation” has gone way over the top. Without Super or Max, the energy system and unskippable ads make the app frustrating to use. Whatever happened to simply doing practice to earn a heart? That actually encouraged me to learn.

I regret paying for the subscription. If you’re considering Duolingo, I’d seriously recommend trying other language-learning apps before spending your money here.

614 day streak btw

title: Very upset
body: I have been on Duolingo for years, and while it used to be good it has really gone downhill lately. It has been pretty  good with helping me learn German, although I feel like after 3 years I should be better at speaking it. And I know it’s not a me problem because I remember everything it teaches me and I do like 3 lessons a day it just teaches you veryyyy slowly. Also they are now using AI to generate sentences, I have noticed multiple times a sentence not making sense, and ive double checked with other sources and they agree it’s incorrect. This company is trying to do as little work as possible and make as much money as possible. This app used to be amazing but it honestly kinda sucks now. Also I am a very fast learner and I feel like the learning is too slow-paced for me, and while I could skip units I don’t really want to, mainly because ever since the German course extension there are so many words it has never taught me and expects me to know, so if I skip units I will probably miss a bunch of content. Also I feel like the vocab it teaches isn’t that helpful. I preferred the original learning path where you could choose what areas you wanted to learn. I think there should be an option to go back to the old learning path. Can the devs please improve the app and stop using AI, I am considering deleting this app and using a different app. Also ENERGY SUCKS. After every lesson I need to watch an add which is really annoying. I prefer hearts. Energy just means more add which means more money for this greedy company. They don’t care about users anymore they only care about being rich. I find the developers behaviour disgusting and I am very disappointed.

title: Free trial expired without notice, silently charged $56
body:
My trial was set to expire on August 19. I opened the app at noon that day to cancel — already charged $56，which is 300 RMB. The charge was processed early that morning, and I received NO prior notice whatsoever. No email. No SMS. No push notification. Nothing.

Here's the thing: August 19 is the ENTIRE expiration day. I tried to cancel at noon — the day wasn't even over. By charging me before the day ended, you effectively took away my right to cancel on the expiration date itself.

And I'm not alone. Tons of users in these reviews report the exact same issue — no notice, silently charged on expiration day, customer service gives no effective response. You know about this problem and you've done nothing to fix it.

$56/300 RMB isn't a fortune, but this practice is just wrong. Your reminder system is broken, but your charging system works like clockwork. Won't be using this app again and won't recommend it to anyone.

Warning: don't start the free trial anyway，even the learing rate is low

title: Great as an addition to class
body:
I’m learning Arabic on Duolingo, and I’ve found it a great accompaniment to do at home alongside class. 
For the Duolingo Arabic course, these are the positives I see: 
- male and female voices so you get used to hearing sounds both ways 
- you can practice letters in a separate tab 
- you can practice with and without sound m, depending on how hard you want it to be 
And here are some things I would suggest: 
- a tab to learn grammar and dictation. A lot of the grammar and connecting words I wouldn’t have known how to do if I wasn’t taking class. 
- sometimes the voices say a long vowel as a short vowel and vice versa 
Overall I think Duolingo is a great resource that is both helpful and fun.

title: “AI Slop” Now, Plus No Customer Support for Paid Subscribers
body:
AI Slop! That's how I would describe the audio component of Duolingo for Japanese and Korean. When you select a single word, it might pronounce it correctly or passably, but in a sentence, the same word is pronounced incorrectly or vice versa. As someone with native-level auditory comprehension, it is alarming to think that some people are learning words by hearing these examples. It is much harder to retrain your ears than to learn a word properly the first time. You have been warned!

Another unforgivable sin in language training is poor samples. Just this week, I had to translate sentences like, “I will help the table tidy up”.  What?  

Speaking exercises are pretty ordinary too. It will not always pick up what has been said; often, a word or two aren’t recognised - using headphones does improve recognition a bit.

Then there is the issue of no support! Not by phone, email, or chat facility. Zero! That's for paid subscribers. We can report issues via the Duolingo app, but I have no idea if it makes a difference. If we are going to be beta testers, perhaps they could reward users with a free, reward extension of our subscription.

Before subscribing to Duolingo, I recommend experiencing these issues for yourself.  If you filter user reviews for ‘most critical’, you will read many users talking about the same AI-related issues.  

If you plan to use the free lessons, I assume your expectations for the level of service will be lower.  

Based on steady degradation of Duolingo over the past two years, I will not recommend this learning tool.  It is more a language game, rather than trusted source of learning.

title: AI is useless, The app is ruined for Japanese language learners
body:
Inconsistent, Unreliable, I now question everything I am being taught. Too many mistakes and bad translation. Nonsensical sentences. Direct translations. Words practice has been wrecked by flashcards. You cover less words as a result. I already have an app for that. Too much hiragana replacements for kanji learnt in previous 6 levels. No more concept introduction or new words. Since AI upgrade I have been bombarded with over a thousand words including verbs. No longer able to track my progress. Considering other apps as I feel utterly disrespected as a customer by Duolingo. Lessons take too long to load or worse yet give an error and don’t work. ￼When you complete the legendary lessons of a unit, after finishing the third last lesson of a unit the last two also turn gold. Lessons can most times are completed after just 4 questions while others can be more than a dozen.. 
No way to communicate errors and faults or give feedback via the app. Completely unacceptable.

title: Untested lessons
body:
Special offers are not shared between devices on the same account. So I got penalised yet again because I had to use my phone instead of my iPad and couldn’t access the 3x reward I set up the day before. It’s been like this for years. Do they never test anything? Another lost tournament. Another day having my butt kicked while being shamed by cartoon characters on Duolingo. I’m learning but it’s so painful. Some of timed reviews are impossible. I challenge a native speaker to finish them in the allotted time. Nor is it possible to review your mistakes afterwards. Where is the pedagogy? I figured I would be ready to go to stage 3 in Greek when I could get through the timed exercises with only 3 strikes. 5 months later, I still can’t do it. At this rate I will complete Greek around Doomsday. Don’t they check pass rates with analytics? The French daily fresh is also an exercise in frustration. It’s like wading through mud. You get it 99% right? Well that’s 100% wrong! How about highlighting the mistake and giving the student a second chance? When I got asked if I wanted to use focus mode, I thought ‘Great, those notifications popping up do distract me. It would be nice to silence them while I’m doing my lessons.’ But no, instead this morning I found half my apps greyed out, including my banking app. I can’t open them til I’ve finished a lesson. So I have to work out how to reverse it. Grrr.  I’ve been subscribed to Duolingo for over 5 years now. Duolingo consistently says I’m in the top 1% of their learners. Every week I rack up about 10,000 points which is enough to rank me 4th -15th in that week’s cohort. The algorithm always pits me against people who do more, so I never even place. The timed challenges are good for drilling it in, but I always fail the same ones. Clearly there’s no data-driven refinement of lessons based on population failure rates. 
It’s so annoying the way the 3x autoactivates. Only got time for a quick lesson before 12 today but would like to set up your reward for a big afternoon session?  Forget it. Duolingo is inflexible.
I’m learning, but it’s so demoralising and anxiety-inducing.

title: Great concept, but an awful cash grab
body: Duolingo is great if you can ignore the obvious staging and setting up to encourage users to buy their premium subscription service which has a ridiculous price. The amount of progress you can make (when not using their extortionate subscription) is determined by how much “battery” you have left. The battery level can drain fast and also randomly changes inbetween lessons with battery life disappearing by substantial amounts even though you never used the sum that disappears for questions. If you can persevere through the desperate attempts to get you to subscribe then it’s fine. But it can be very discouraging when it’s setting you up to fail in order to encourage you to subscribe. ☹️

title: Feedback & Suggestions
body: Duolingo is such a great language learning app that everyone should get if they are learning a language. I am currently doing French and my skills have improved so much and it has also helped me with my French assessments at school. Here are some suggestions to this app: 1. Sometimes I accidentally press on the continue button when I haven't finished my sentence yet, so maybe add another button where I can undo to finish my sentence. 2. Add maybe this thing where you can buy with gems, which makes up one day for the streak, because sometimes I have school camp, and I can't bring moblile, so I wouldn't be able to do my streak. 3. Add this thing where I can type in a topic that I can focus on, because I have assessments, and having this would help me a lot it and, this can be like a side dish in the app, where the main dish would still be the normal course. Overall, Duolingo is a great languages app and please consider my suggestions!

title: Used to be good, not anymore
body:
The more things are updated, the worse they get, both the app and the courses. UI inconsistencies, speech not triggering, or triggering really late, wrong voice being used, etc.

On the course side, at least for Japanese, it no longer finds the correct word boundaries, it inserts long pauses in speech where there should be none (word boundary issue?), jumps all over the place in difficulty, and has some really questionable translations and phrasings that even I as a beginner pick up on.

It didn't help that they completely revamped the course material and provided a terrible catch-up section that was woefully incomplete, but that is minor in comparison to the other issues.

It is no longer an app that I can use for learning, and I say that as someone who just uninstalled it with a 1200+ day streak. Needless to say, I won't renew my subscription either.

So I’m not saying Duolingo is BAD, but why do we run out of energy so quickly? Why does it take forever to recharge? Why is it when I say “Yes, I’m gonna finish this lesson!” This stupid bird comes to me and says, “Oh No! YoU’vE rAn OuT oF eNeRgY!” Like bro, let me finish my lesson gng😭✌️🥀🥀

For this, I call Duolingo P2W (Pay to win). It’s not really winning, but I DO NOT want to see this stupid bird come to my face and ask for like $150 for no ads and unlimited energy, like serious blud🗣️🔥🔥.

Sure, it’s cool that when u reach a goal of like 7 days streak u get one for 3 days but then it reminds u of what u have to deal with as a F2P (free to play) person afterwards.

Thank you Duolingo for helping me learn, but please, stop it and let me learn in peace bro.

title: Constant ads
body: The app goes through basics, but then it puts “gems” “experience” annoying reminders to install widgets, allow emails, notifications.  I love being reminded, but I don’t want to open my email and get an email saying so, or be forced to do extra steps to be reminded like installing widgets.  Then, there’s the constant ads and limitations on learning, because you use energy you’re limited on how much you can learn. If you only have 5 minutes a lesson is great.  But what if I have an hour?  Then mid lesson, that it’s asked you to do, you run out of energy, and suddenly you don’t get to continue.  All pushing you to pay for a service which frankly, there are better alternatives too.

title: Explain my answer has disappeared & deceptive advertiser methods
body:
Why has “explain my answer” disappeared from my app ?

The advertising is becoming unacceptable

I enjoy using Duolingo, but the advertising experience has become a serious problem.

In particular, I repeatedly encounter ads from a Chinese online retailer where the apparent X/close button is effectively a hidden link. Instead of closing the advertisement, tapping the X can open the advertiser’s website in my browser and leave cookies behind. I have also encountered similar behaviour where tapping what appears to be the volume/control area triggers the advertisement.

This feels like deceptive advertising design rather than a legitimate way of closing an ad. A close button should close the ad — it should not unexpectedly open an external website.

Because of this, I now avoid watching the advertisements in Duolingo altogether. It’s particularly frustrating because I otherwise enjoy the app.

Duolingo needs to take responsibility for the advertising it serves and ensure that ads cannot use misleading or disguised touch targets to redirect users to external websites.

title: Terrible
body:
I spent 330 days learning Russian on Duolingo, along with studying German, and honestly, I have to ask: what exactly did I learn?

The Russian alphabet is a perfect example of how badly this app teaches. Russian uses an entirely different alphabet, yet Duolingo barely taught me how to properly recognize and read the letters. Instead, I was thrown into lessons and expected to somehow figure things out along the way.

Because of that, almost every Russian lesson feels like a guessing game. I’m not confidently answering because I understand the language—I’m guessing which answer Duolingo wants me to pick and hoping I somehow got it right. That’s not learning a language. That’s trying to survive a multiple-choice quiz.

And then there’s German. I tried putting my German skills to the test with someone who actually speaks German fluently, and I discovered that some of the things I had learned from Duolingo didn’t exactly hold up in real-life conversation.

Without Premium, good luck learning without constantly dealing with ads, hearts, restrictions, and interruptions. The app starts feeling less like a language-learning platform and more like a subscription advertisement with a language course attached.

Duolingo is incredibly good at making you feel like you’re progressing. You get XP, streaks, levels, celebrations, and a green owl acting like you’ve achieved linguistic greatness. Meanwhile, after 330 days, I still don’t feel confident reading the Russian alphabet, and I feel like I’m guessing my way through lessons.

At this point, I’m not learning Russian. I’m maintaining a streak and hoping the green owl doesn’t come after me.

1/10. More interested in keeping you on the app than actually making you fluent.

content.label:
I spent 330 days learning Russian on Duolingo, along with studying German, and honestly, I have to ask: what exactly did I learn?

The Russian alphabet is a perfect example of how badly this app teaches. Russian uses an entirely different alphabet, yet Duolingo barely taught me how to properly recognize and read the letters. Instead, I was thrown into lessons and expected to somehow figure things out along the way.

Because of that, almost every Russian lesson feels like a guessing game. I’m not confidently answering because I understand the language—I’m guessing which answer Duolingo wants me to pick and hoping I somehow got it right. That’s not learning a language. That’s trying to survive a multiple-choice quiz.

And then there’s German. I tried putting my German skills to the test with someone who actually speaks German fluently, and I discovered that some of the things I had learned from Duolingo didn’t exactly hold up in real-life conversation.

Without Premium, good luck learning without constantly dealing with ads, hearts, restrictions, and interruptions. The app starts feeling less like a language-learning platform and more like a subscription advertisement with a language course attached.

At this point, I’m not learning Russian. I’m maintaining a streak and hoping the green owl doesn’t come after me.

1/10. More interested in keeping you on the app than actually making you fluent.

title: Stop Promoting LGBT Themes in Language Lessons

Duolingo has gone far beyond simply teaching languages. Its lessons repeatedly include same-sex relationships and LGBT-related themes to such an extent that it feels less like neutral representation and more like deliberate promotion.

I downloaded Duolingo to learn a language, not to be repeatedly exposed to social and ideological messaging. Duolingo should focus on language education and give users a clear option to disable this type of content.

title: Not the same as it used to be
body: I have been on Duolingo for over three years and over 1000 days of learning and although I still can’t speak the language lol, I did prefer Duolingo over other apps. Recently though, it has been getting stuck on a lesson at the same point and you can’t choose the correct answer, so you can’t move on any further. Then you close the lesson and start again the same thing happens at the same spot. I’ve closed the lesson and tried multiple times and it doesn’t move past that point. I then deleted the app and reinstalled it and it was okay for a couple days and is now doing the same thing again. Nothing like this has happened in over three years. Also, I do love the new flashcards in the quiz, but recently it has been giving me words that I’ve never even practiced in the regular lessons (about 90%) of the words, so it makes it nearly impossible to move forward. Before it would give you words that you have practiced or are at least starting to learn. It’s very frustrating and I hope they can fix these bugs because they don’t reply to emails.

title: The Taliban Ban Education. What’s Duolingo’s Excuse?
body:
I am deeply disappointed by Duolingo’s decision to make its English Test unavailable to people in Iran.

Your app supports countless languages, yet Persian, spoken by millions of people, is still absent. Now, on top of that, people in Iran are being excluded from taking an English proficiency test that can be crucial for access to education.

Education should never be restricted based on nationality. Denying an entire population access to an educational service solely because they are in Iran is discriminatory, regardless of the justification behind the policy.

The Taliban have become notorious for restricting Afghan girls’ access to education. That mentality, excluding an entire group of people from educational opportunities because of who they are, should have no place anywhere. What is particularly disturbing is seeing a form of collective educational exclusion coming from a company based in a country that presents itself as committed to equality and access to education.

You do not have to be in Afghanistan to reproduce the logic of exclusion from education.

It is shameful to see an education company treating an entire nationality this way. Duolingo should reconsider this policy and explain why Iranian test takers are being collectively excluded.

title: Discrimination by Nationality
body: I’ve used Duolingo for many years and took the Duolingo English Test for university admission. As of Sept 1, the test is banned in Iran: fine, that follows US sanctions, BUT Duolingo went further and banned everyone with an Iranian ID trying to take the test anywhere in the world, even people living abroad trying to take the test or travelling abroad to take it. US sanctions target residents of Iran, not people of Iranian nationality anywhere in the world. That makes this second ban not compliance, but discrimination by nationality, a company choosing convenience over ordinary people trying to get an education and build a better life. I’m deleting the app. I will revise this review if Duolingo limits the restriction to what the law actually requires.

title: Extremely disappointing and unfair treatment of Iranian candidates
body:
Duolingo should explain why Iranian candidates are being prevented from accessing or continuing with the English proficiency test. English proficiency is an academic and professional requirement, and candidates should not be disadvantaged simply because of their nationality or where they are located.

If there are legal or sanctions-related restrictions affecting Duolingo English Test availability in Iran, Duolingo should provide a clear, transparent explanation and, where possible, offer a fair alternative for legitimate students and applicants.

Blocking or discontinuing access without adequate explanation can have serious consequences for students whose university applications, immigration plans, or careers depend on an English proficiency score.

I hope Duolingo reviews this policy and provides a transparent solution for Iranian candidates who are simply trying to demonstrate their English ability.

title: Discrimination Has No Place in Education
body:
Discriminating against Iranian users based on their nationality is deeply disappointing and unacceptable. Education should never be restricted because of where someone was born.

Duolingo presents itself as a platform that makes language learning accessible to everyone, but excluding Iranian users completely contradicts that mission. If you truly believe education and language learning should be available to all, your policies should reflect those values.

And honestly, this decision is not entirely surprising. Despite having a large number of Iranian users for years, Duolingo has still never added Persian (Farsi) to its supported languages. That already felt exclusionary, and this latest decision only reinforces the impression that Iranian users are being treated differently.

Access to education should bring people together, not become another tool for discrimination. Duolingo should seriously reconsider this decision and treat Iranian users with the same fairness and respect as everyone else.

Access to education should be based on merit and ability—not nationality.

For years, Duolingo promoted accessibility and equal educational opportunities. Denying access to an English proficiency test for an entire group of students contradicts those values. Education should build bridges, not create new barriers. Restricting students from pursuing academic and professional opportunities because of where they were born is unfair and discouraging. 

I hope Duolingo reconsiders this decision and works toward a solution that supports learners rather than excluding them.

title: Unfair ban based on nationality
body:
Extremely disappointed that Duolingo now blocks Iranian users from taking the Duolingo English Test. 
This isn’t about individual eligibility, it’s a blanket ban based purely on nationality and ID documents. 
Duolingo used to stand for accessible, equal education for everyone, and this policy goes against that completely.
Thousands of my Iranian friends who are students rely on this test for university and job applications worldwide. Shutting them out because of where they were born is unfair and honestly heartbreaking for people who worked hard to get here.
Please reconsider this policy, Duolingo. Find a way to support these learners instead of excluding them entirely. 
1 star until this changes.

title: Absolutely unacceptable and discriminatory.
body:
Duolingo claims to make English testing accessible to people “anywhere in the world,” yet it is now denying Iranian students access to the Duolingo English Test simply because of where they are from or because they have an Iranian-issued ID.

Students should be judged based on their English proficiency and abilities — not their nationality or the country that issued their ID.

This is especially unfair to Iranian students who are studying, applying to universities, or building their future abroad. Education should not be used as a political tool, and innocent students should not be punished for decisions made by governments.

Blocking an entire group of students from an educational opportunity is discriminatory and deeply disappointing. Let students be judged by their abilities, not their nationality.

title: Education is not a sanction
body:
I used Duolingo to learn languages, and I paid for Super. The lessons work. That is not why I am writing.
On 1 September 2026 the same company stopped the Duolingo English Test for people in Iran and for people who hold Iranian ID — including those living outside Iran. TOEFL already closed testing inside Iran. Duolingo went further and tied the ban to identity, not only to location.
Students are not a government. They are trying to apply to university. A language company that sells “education for everyone” should not collect subscription money from the same community it locks out of an official exam.
I am canceling Super. I will keep learning English. I will not keep paying a company that treats an Iranian ID as a reason to close the door.
Education should not be denied by nationality.

title: Please Fix This!
body: I am a dedicated user who loves learning on your platform, but recent changes have significantly impacted the experience. While it is wonderful that you support rare languages, major global languages like Farsi and comprehensive Mandarin courses are still missing from the catalog, which misses out on millions of potential learners. Furthermore, replacing the traditional heart mechanic with the new energy system severely disrupts the learning flow by forcing users to either stop studying or pay to continue. The constant pressure from advertisements, premium subscriptions, gem purchases, and paid invites makes the app feel overly transactional, shifting the focus from genuine education to aggressive upselling. I understand the need for a profitable business model, but these heavy paywalls penalize dedicated students. Please consider rebalancing these features so language learning remains truly accessible.

body: Followed a link for a one week free trial and was charged immediately for a full year’s subscription. Was told in an automated AI email response to reach out to Apple for a resolution. There is no way to speak to an actual person who might actually care that their app may have malfunctioned. I didn’t accidentally sign up. I was prompted by the app with an offer that included a choice of “remind me 2 or 3 days” prior to the trial ending. That is what I clicked on and agreed to. I was charged immediately. Maybe that was an error on Apple’s end, I don’t know. You’d think  Duolingo might want to know for sure instead of passing blame or making convenient assumptions. A real representative with critical thinking skills might be required here. The app itself may well have been worth it, but there is no trust is the company or its commitment to the customers that clearly pay them a lot of money. Leaving a negative review feels very “Karen” to me - yet it’s an honest unsatisfactory experience that wasn’t addressed

A real representative with critical thinking skills might be required here. The app itself may well have been worth it, but there is no trust is the company or its commitment to the customers that clearly pay them a lot of money. title: Cheap Provocation
body:
It is genuinely astonishing that the team who wrote and approved Oscar’s dialogue, especially in the chess section, could have such a poor understanding of the difference between education and cheap provocation.

This character is not clever, funny, or competitive. It is simply childish, irritating, and obnoxious. What is even more embarrassing is that someone wrote these lines, someone else reviewed them, and they still collectively decided, “Yes, this is what we should show users.”

Chess is a game of discipline, respect, and composure. You somehow managed to insert into it dialogue that feels like it was written by a child in a middle-school hallway, poking people just to get a reaction.

If I were on the team responsible for this feature, I would be embarrassed to put it on my résumé. What you created is not just a badly written character; it is a small showcase of how shallow your understanding of user psychology, education, and humor appears to be.

An educational app trying to keep users engaged by irritating them when it can no longer engage them through the quality of its teaching is a remarkable product vision—and not in a way anyone should be proud of.

title: Very Disappointed by Duolingo’s Shameless Marketing Tactics
body:
I’ve been using Duolingo for three years, but honestly, I’ve lost my trust in it as an educational app.

Duolingo seems willing to go to any length for attention with its marketing. What really bothers me is that this has included repeatedly making jokes about the private life of a well-known singer who has absolutely nothing to do with Duolingo. In the Chinese context, these references are very recognizable and hurtful not only to the singer, but also to his fans and family.

On July 6, 2025, Duolingo posted controversial remarks on its official Douyin account. After public backlash, the content was deleted. Yet on September 9, 2026, it posted  the exactly same remarks again on its official Xiaohongshu (RedNote) account, despite already knowing the controversy surrounding them.

After three years as a user, I’m honestly very disappointed. I can no longer trust Duolingo as an educational platform when its marketing repeatedly puts attention before basic respect.
对多邻国近期在网络平台的一些营销和内容处理方式非常失望。

作为一个语言学习平台，我认为基本的尊重和责任感应该体现在官方营销中。尤其是涉及现实中与软件无关的人物、公众人物及其粉丝群体时，官方平台更应该谨慎处理，避免使用容易产生特定指向、误导或伤害性的表达。

如果一个营销内容能够让大量用户明确联想到特定人物，并进一步对该人物、其粉丝乃至家人造成负面影响，那么这已经不只是“开玩笑”或者“营销创意”的问题，而是值得认真反思的内容审核和品牌责任问题。

一个教育平台应该对自己的公开内容承担相应责任，也应该重视不同文化语境下表达可能产生的实际影响。而不是在2025年7月6日抖音平台官方账号所发信息已经引发巨大舆论争议的情况下，明知故犯的在2026年9月9日小红书平台再次发布相同的争议引导性言论。

作为一位使用了三年的用户，我无法再信任将多邻国作为教育软件使用。

title: Only good if you pay for it.
body:
So I’ve been using Duolingo for a few months at this point, learning French.

The app itself has a decent cycle of learning. With the French side, you practice speaking, reading, and listening to French and sometimes applying what you’ve learned in simple scenarios to get a better feel for the words being used.

The problem is the app is designed to make you upgrade to their subscription at every possible opportunity. Finished a lesson? Here’s an ad. Run out of energy? (Energy only lasts 1 to 2 lessons without a refill at most), watch some ads. Want to talk to our AI? That’s behind the paywall.

Even when they’ve given me free previews, it still has frustrated me to use. The AI takes a French immersion approach (aside from Falstaff who asks you questions in the native language), meaning asking for help isn’t easy, and when you try, does not appear on the transcript after the lesson correctly.

Overall, it has a solid baseline to learn French, but if you’re serious about learning a language, you’re better off finding humans to learn from.

title: Gamification is ruining actual learning
body:
I have a 240-day streak and just finished level 52 of the French course as a paying super user, I’m incredibly frustrated with the recent updates. The app has completely shifted its focus from actual language education to aggressive gamification.

Firstly, a recent course update dropped a massive wave of completely new vocabulary,  verbs and completely new sentence structure, all at once and with very little repetition and exercises on how to use them. They have also removed the dedicated grammar and sentence explanations for these, so I’m left guessing complex French grammas rules rather than learning.

At the same time, they create intense pressure with leagues, leaderboard finals and XP farming, encouraging users to rush through content to keep up. The app actively rewards speed over actual comprehension and retention.

I pay for a subscription to learn a language not to play an unbalanced game. Please bring back proper grammar guides, explaining of answers and fix the lesson pacing.

For anyone considering using the app to learn a language, I’d recommend to not pay for this app but rather spend your money on an app like Babbel that takes your learning seriously

Duolingo has introduced a policy preventing people with Iranian identification documents from taking the Duolingo English Test, effectively excluding Iranian applicants regardless of where they live or their individual circumstances.

title: Discrimination
body:
I am deeply disappointed by Duolingo's decision to block
Iranian users from taking the Duolingo English Test. This policy punishes students and academic applicants based solely on their nationality and identification documents, regardless of their individual circumstances.
For years, Duolingo promoted accessibility and equal educational opportunities.
Denying access to an English proficiency test for an entire group of students contradicts those values. Many Iranian students rely on this exam because it is affordable and widely accepted by universities around the world.
Education should build bridges, not create new barriers. Restricting students from pursuing academic and professional opportunities because of where they were born is unfair and discouraging.
I hope Duolingo reconsiders this decision and works toward a solution that
supports learners rather than excluding them.

title: Racism against Iranian nation!!!
body:
Duolingo has spent years positioning itself as a champion of accessibility and equal access to education. Shutting an entire group of students out of an English proficiency test sits badly with that message. For many Iranian students, this exam matters precisely because it is affordable and recognised by universities worldwide.

Education ought to open doors rather than close them. Blocking students from academic and professional opportunities on the basis of where they happened to be born is both unjust and demoralising.

I would urge Duolingo to revisit this decision and find an approach that supports learners instead of shutting them out.

title: My experience with Duolingo is mixed
body:
I like the concept and the gamification, but I often felt that entertainment, speed and collecting points were prioritised over the actual quality of learning.
The AI language conversations lacked depth and therefore did not feel particularly natural or useful. At one point, the AI even guessed that I was 12 years old, although I am an adult, which gave me the impression that the app is primarily aimed at children of that age. I also completed most of the chess section, where Duolingo claimed that I had reached 1100 ELO, while my actual Chess.com rating only went up to around 500, making their rating rather misleading.

Some recurring stories also surprised me, as characters who make little effort in learning are sometimes given recognition, while those who put in effort are sidelined. Passive-aggressive conversations also feature quite significantly, and I did not enjoy learning or being exposed to this style of communication.

The league system can also be demotivating: even after investing a lot of time in learning, you can be pushed down to a lower league. In tournaments, rewards often seem to favour whoever completes exercises fastest or earns the biggest point boosts, rather than whoever has actually learned the most.

Overall, Duolingo may be entertaining or useful for younger or casual learners, but for an adult looking for deeper and more meaningful knowledge, natural conversation and a fair measure of progress, I think there is considerable room for improvement.

title: It’s good, but very American
body:
I have found the process of learning in Duolingo good. I managed to complete the entire Latin offering, learning how to describe parrots as being drunk. These last few months I’ve been learning Spanish, and it has been useful when visiting Spain on holiday, in fact it’s been very useful.
However, the heavy American influence is jarring. As an English speaker, I do not use dollars, I have no time for baseball, basketball doesn’t register in my vocabulary, and football is football, not soccer. All these Americanisms do nothing for visiting Spain. They genuinely get in the way of learning a new language because they do not translate well to English.
Given the clear hard work and effort put in by the Duolingo teams to create what is a good product, it seems a shame to have missed out on the very real and striking localisation differences. If you’re American learning Mexican, then I’m sure it’s brilliant, but if you’re English learning Spanish then it’s still good, don’t get me wrong, but it will jar a little as you have to stop and retranslate. Please replace baseball with cricket or some local Spanish alternative that would enable your users to make connections with native Spanish speakers. Thank you though. Overall I do enjoy Duolingo.

title: Calm down, Duo!
body:
Duo is a little too needy and impatient. If I don't practice immediately, the constant stream of notifications starts: "Do you know what time it is?", "Are you awake?", "I'm impatient!", "Will you be back soon?"
It genuinely starts to feel like being in a clingy relationship.
Please calm down, Duo. I'd love the option to practise on my own schedule instead of feeling pressured by endless reminders. Unlocking offline mode would make the experience much more enjoyable, allowing me to learn when I can rather than when the app decides I should.
A little less clingy, a little more flexibility, and I'd be much more likely to keep coming back.

title: Okay but…
body:
Duolingo is probably one of the most well known language learning apps ever, but I have been using it for a few years know are there are some things that I really wish could change: 

1. On Duolingo you can turn on notifications for it to remind you to keep your streak. At first I thought this was a good idea until it started notifying me every ten minutes from very early in the morning to ridiculously late at night. 

2. I don’t personally think it helps very much with learning a language as you are so pressed into saving your streak that you just rush through the lessons and don’t pay much attention.

3. Something that I find incredibly stupid is the “energy”. If you do not have super Duolingo, you have limited energy and if you use it all up, you cannot complete a lesson. So either you pay or you can only do one lesson a day and therefore don’t really learn anything.

4. If you don’t have much time to do a lesson, the lessons are a reasonable length but after that it is so long as you have to collect chests, watch the really long ads and get placed on a leaderboard.

So finally, I would say, keep looking for another language learning app. As this one is not very educational.

title: Broken activities
body: Haven’t tried other languages but been trying to learn Latin on the free version for the past 90 days on ios26 iPad and find it very frustrating due to poor programming. There are so many broken activities with buttons that don’t select, or don’t produce any sound. Very frustrating to get half way through an activity then find you’re going to be penalised for not being able to complete it when half the buttons on a pairs activity don’t actually select. Have tried using the browser version on Win 11 - the rewards are much lower than on the app which makes it difficult to gain enough points to continue. Timing isn’t adjustable which is very frustrating when you run out of time because something won’t click. Random Latin words appear on the English word buttons when you’re asked to select words in English. Wouldn’t buy the paid for version of this app due to the number of errors in the Latin version. Have reported them but no change. Could be so much better.

title: Excellent if you do more than the daily minimum
body:
Duolingo’s superpower is the gamification of language learning, it will keep you at it. But to succeed at anything more than a snail’s pace you’ll want to do multiple lessons per day and ensure it’s not your only resource.

As a feature request, I would simply like to be able to CHOOSE specific vocabulary (e.g. family members, fruit, vehicles, etc) for flashcard practice.

Aim to get five friends on a family subscription with you, this is not really supposed to be free software if you want results.

Duolingo is very good and I suspect it will only get better.

title: Incessant adverts
body:
The free plan is totally infuriating with the incessant adverts. 
The paid plan also suffers from constant upselling to the max plan. I’ve already paid so stop ramming upselling into the experience. It never used to be like this. Just stop it, Duo. title: I’m a bit middling on it

It also says that you can have a free trial and then stop but when I did it it said I had to pay or it would delete the app! So that gets half a star taken away. So I guess, some people like it, some do not.

title: Interactive but falls short for particular courses
body:
I used Duolingo to learn Scottish Gaelic. The course ended very abruptly. Some big grammar concepts are barely touched upon. I was very sad to learn that Scottish Gaelic is not receiving any further investment to develop it. That’s interesting because Duolingo claims to care about endangered languages. Most people in my face-to-face Gaelic class all use Duolingo and people are relying on it to keep the language alive. However there are most definitely gaps in the course in terms of content, and interactivity. For example Gaelic has no speaking function, and no fun games like maths, and French.
About the app more generally, XP boosts encourage the user to speed through lessons rather than learning content and there are definitely bots on the league tables.

title: Improvements to Italian course
body: There are two major problems. The first is that genders should always be learnt alongside the noun so that the correct agreement comes more naturally. There is also a lot of ambiguity in the translation flashcards, especially with infinitives, which should be prefaced by ‘to’, feminine/masculine forms of the same noun and words that have several meanings. I often feel I need to be a mind reader. Additionally, it would be good to be able to bank extra points for later in the day, if you have to go out/do something else when you have just gained a lot of extra XPs.

title: Pure unfair Duo/ Sick of the paywalls 🤬
body:
Pure greed / Sick of the paywalls 🤬

I am sick and tired of this app hiding every single useful feature behind an expensive paywall. Locking the new AI Video Calls and Roleplay features behind Duolingo Max is an absolute joke. Free users are left with the bare minimum while super, super fam, and max users hoard all the actual conversational tools for profit.
And also, you already force us to watch endless ads and constantly pressure us to buy Super Duolingo. Making a whole new, even more expensive tier just to gatekeep the best learning tools is a blatant cash grab. You already reward users with 3 free days of Super Duolingo when they hit milestones or do really well in their course—why can't you do the exact same thing with Max? Let free users earn a few days of AI features through hard work. Stop being unfair and give everyone access to modern speaking practice. Apart from that I find Duolingo a nice learning app but Duo, you NEED to improve.🦉❌

title: Here learning and playing go hand in hand
body:
I am learning Portuguese and Chess on Duolingo!!! I learn  Portuguese which is nothing but fun packed tasks which literally makes you start speaking the language in a month. With listening and speaking tasks with their virtual fun animated staffs. After every class they will praise you, which takes you to the top of the world. 
Then I play and learn chess. My ultimate goal here is to beat my chess genius brother. You get to learn math and music here too! 
They have a fun way of reminding you to take your daily classes . All you have to do is keep your notifications on for this. They have a monthly scorecard with all the participants which motivates you to be on the top list. For the first few months I didn’t have the super Duolingo. But this type of learning becomes so addictive that I had to take the subscription and honestly it was a worth it purchase for me. 
You can use this app without the subscription but the function of the app is soo good it will force you to take the subscriptions. 

Regards,
A Happy learner

title: Best language learning app ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
body:
Duolingo is one of the best language-learning apps I have ever used. It makes learning a new language fun, simple, and enjoyable for people of all ages. The lessons are short and interactive, so it is easy to practice every day without feeling overwhelmed. Each lesson includes reading, listening, speaking, and writing activities that help improve language skills step by step. The app also teaches new vocabulary, pronunciation, sentence structure, and basic grammar in a way that is easy to understand.

One of the best features of Duolingo is its game-like design. Learners can earn points, unlock achievements, complete daily goals, and maintain streaks, which makes practicing every day exciting and motivating. The colorful animations and friendly characters make the lessons more enjoyable, especially for children and beginners. The app also allows users to learn at their own pace, making it suitable for both busy students and adults.

Another great advantage is that Duolingo offers many different languages, giving users the chance to explore cultures from around the world. The app provides instant feedback whenever a mistake is made, helping learners understand and correct their errors immediately. It also tracks progress over time, making it easy to see how much you have improved.

Although Duolingo is an excellent learning tool, it is best used along with real conversations, books, videos, and other resources to become fluent in a language. Overall, Duolingo is a fantastic app that makes language learning enjoyable, effective, and easy to fit into daily life. I would happily recommend it to anyone who wants to learn a new language or improve their language skills. 5 out of 5 stars.

title: Match Madness
body:
I used to really enjoy Match Madness because it was a fun and effective way to test vocabulary, speed, and recall. Unfortunately, after the last 3-4 updates in about one month of time, the experience has become noticeably less enjoyable.
The main issue is the timing and synchronisation of the matching words. Even when you are selecting the correct words quickly, the corresponding options sometimes do not appear at the same pace. On some occasions, I have experienced a delay of nearly 2 seconds before the matching word appears. Since the game is time-limited to 1 minute 45 seconds and requires rapid responses, these delays can easily lead to mistakes and make the experience frustrating rather than challenging.
Match Madness was one of the best features of Duolingo for me, but currently it feels like a great feature has been compromised by the recent updates. I sincerely hope the timing and synchronisation issues can be addressed soon. If feature can not be made responsive and consistent, it may be better to reconsider or redesign the mode rather than leave it in its current state.
I genuinely enjoy Duolingo and hope the team will look into this. The best thing has gone bad- I really hope to see Match Madness brought back to its former quality. Hoping for the Best!

title: Please Bring Sanskrit to Duolingo!
body:
I love Duolingo and would really like to see a Sanskrit course added.

Sanskrit is one of the world’s oldest and most influential languages, with an extraordinary body of literature spanning philosophy, mathematics, science, poetry, linguistics, and history. Yet for most people, learning Sanskrit still has a very high barrier to entry.

Duolingo could change that. A well-designed Sanskrit course could make the language approachable for millions of people in India and around the world, including complete beginners.

It would help people explore important historical texts in their original language, understand the roots of many Indian languages, and engage with a remarkable linguistic and cultural heritage.

Please consider making Sanskrit accessible to everyone through Duolingo. I would sign up on day one! 🙏

title: Max video call isn't worth it
body:
I really enjoy Duolingo, but there are a few frustrating issues with the AI video calls with Lily. If you receive a phone call or briefly switch to another app to reply to a message, the entire call progress is lost. There’s also no option to pause, stop, or save partial progress, even when a call can last more than 10 minutes.

There should also be an option to interrupt or stop the AI when it keeps talking, especially when it has misunderstood a word or the learner wants to correct something.

Another useful improvement would be allowing the AI to understand a few words from another language when necessary. For example, while practicing French, if the learner uses an English word because they don’t know the French equivalent, the AI should understand the context rather than treating it as completely wrong.



Without doing the lessons to learn the new words and grammar. I'm asked to do the final lesson.
I moved ahead to the next unit but same issue there.
This happened after they switched the French path.

But there is a lot of bugs in the app, whenever I try to complete a lesson it just kicks me out,and when I try to complete that same lesson again,it’s kicking me out again. Duolingo, please fix this so that others learners like me don’t miss out on words just because of a minor glitch.

title: Extremely frustrating! Not worth the time
body: I am an English speaker and also relatively fluent in Spanish, and I wanted to learn French to keep up language learning after school. I tried Duolingo and it has so many issues. First, the introductory lessons are all THE SAME. I wasted my time on four basically identical lessons, with absolutely no progression, and sitting through ads between each one. Plus, not only are there ads between each one, there are four different versions of “power up!” “New quest!” “XP earned!” “Recharged your battery!” OH MY GOD PICK ONE AND STICK TO IT!! I feel I’m being bombarded with dopamine but in reality I would be happier if it just said Good Job and moved on!! Nobody using this app is two years old and needs badges and stars every other second. Also, the family plan it keeps advertising is for *presumably* a kid, parent, and FOUR FRIENDS. Where am I supposed to find FIVE MORE PEOPLE TO ALSO JOIN DUOLINGO?? I think that the app creators have to realize that not every user of the app is five years old with an extensive community of people also wanting to learn on an app bombarded with ads and random boosts. I’ve been using the app for 4 days and have not gotten past “yes, a coffee please.” Not to mention how it started threatening to lose my progress on a lesson because I hadn’t paid. Have app makers realize that that’s more of a deterrent, or am I just a genius?      I will now be teaching myself through a textbook.

title: No longer usable with voiceover
body:
I have thoroughly enjoyed using Duolingo for Almost 6 years and in the past it has always worked extremely well with VoiceOver for blind Users. I am totally blind and I’ve been able to use Duolingo successfully until recent releases. With recent updates, The Section review vocabulary flashcards do not work with speech. They did in the past and the similar exercises within lessons work just fine.
With voiceover, my screen says, translate the words and record, but I cannot read the words to be translated. This should be a simple fix and it’s very frustrating that I mentioned it sometime ago and there have been several releases without a fix. I have been unable to p progress in learning Spanish with Duolingo, and will soon run out of lessons to review and will be unable to use the app for anything. It’s extremely annoying to find myself unable to use an app i’ve happily used for years  for want of a simple fix.

title: Relentless advertising and sky high costs…
body: At one point, Duolingo was phenomenal, but the app has taken a massive hit in regard to user experience. I’ll be deleting my account and the application.

title: Love the idea, hate the manipulation
body:
I understand the free version of apps come with commercials and limited features, but Duolingo goes too far pushing their paid version. My kids were left in tears multiple times because they were stressed about losing their streaks and couldn’t complete their lessons without upgrading. The sinister looking characters when you’re at risk of losing your streak are also obnoxious/a source of anxiety for kids. 

From what I’ve read, the paid version isn’t worth the cost and it all feels like a sham to lessen a language after a few minutes a day.

title: AI Fizzles & Frustrates
body:
To let you know I’ve been at this awhile and seen a lot of change… I first heard about this App at a TEDx Conference years ago and loved the concept along with a simple “captcha” technology used to translate written text and make it accessible in many languages online. 

I’m hoping that the game streaks and competition have NOT taken precedence over being able to read, write, hear, and speak a given language well. 

Before all the AI seemed to take over, the App seemed more consistent. As I continue to find inconsistencies that persist, the learning experience has grown frustrating and I’m starting to wonder, “Am I really speaking Spanish with anything close to 90+% accuracy the App suggests?”

Although difficult to capture all the issues when you’re running through a timed lesson and focusing on learning, following 
are some of the issues I’ve experienced a lot, so they’re in my memory. Hope you’ll consider fixing them and continue to stay on top of any new ones. 

Flashcard lessons seem to randomly require “el” or “la” before a term that doesn’t start with “the” in English. Also, “finally” randomly requires “al fin” response and accepts nothing else. Falstaff still periodically uses an American accent in video calls when he’s speaking Spanish.

More sentence responses in Spanish are being counted as errors when a different verb that means the same thing in English is used. Most frustrating are that NOT all mistakes are explained, so we can understand how to speak the language better. 

One improvement that stands out is that sentences with “you” in English are no longer counted as errors if usted, ustedes, or tu are used as long as they’re with the correct verb forms and sentence structure.

title: This app constantly harasses you—even if you’re a paying customer.
body:
I actually like using Duolingo to learn, but the constant upselling and nagging have become ridiculous. I’m a paying customer.  Every day I’m asked to turn on notifications, enable some feature, or upgrade. I say no, and rather than respecting my answer, Duolingo simply asks me again the next day. No means no.

And now they’ve taken the passive-aggressive behavior even further. If you don’t complete enough lessons, the Duolingo icon on your phone changes to a sad, angry, or otherwise disgruntled version of Duo. It feels less like encouragement and more like the app is trying to guilt or manipulate me into using it.

I’m a paying customer. I shouldn’t have to continually dismiss upsells, notifications, and guilt trips just to use a product I’ve already paid for.

This is no way to treat customers. Duolingo needs to stop harassing its paying users and start respecting their choices.

I think “No means no” is particularly effective here because it captures your biggest complaint: you already answered the notification/upgrade question, and they keep asking anyway.

title: Money Grabber App
body:
This app is not as easy to use as it used to be. You see, you have an energy saver now. This wouldn’t be an issue, if it wasn’t completely useless. 
The energy meter only goes to 25. So you would think the lessons would cost you like an energy or two, to do proper lessons, but no. The lessons cost 15 energy, which means you can only do a single lesson a day, because the energy recharges only after 24 hours.
There are ways around this. You get a free +5 energy every hour, and you can also watch ads for +5 energy. However, this becomes aggravating, since you’d have to claim the +5 free and watch an ad, do a lesson, watch two +5 recharge ads, do a lesson. These ads give the app money, which would be the only way to make profit as a large portion of the app’s subscription members were not pleased with the 2024/2025 AI use.
Oh, but the subscription is also where the other half of the money grab comes in, because with a subscription you get UNLIMITED energy. 🫩
The app would be much less aggravating if they would raise the limit on the energizer. So that we could get at least three or four lessons in before we ever have to use ads (because you ALSO see ads at the end of EVERY lesson no matter what). And maybe so that we can make mistakes without having to wait to correct them…? Especially on the time limited lessons, where some people are just unable to match the amount of words under 1 minute and 45 seconds.

title: Way too many ads makes it hard to learn for free.
body: This app use to be good but not it’s obvious they just want you to subscribe to super duolingo just to even use it. Not only are you getting ads after every lesson but you also use up your charge in like 1-2 lessons. Then the ad even throws ridiculous statistics like “super duolingo users learn 5x faster” yeah when the free version only lets you do maybe 2 lessons a day of course subscribers are gonna learn faster 🤣😂. What an epic fail of an ad that one is, but what really kills this app is the new charge system. Before it was hearts you would get 3 and you could keep learning as long as you didn’t miss anything. They obviously didnt like the fact that people were actually learning for free this way cause they completely changed it. Now you get 24 units of charge that take 1 hour to charge 1 unit meaning it takes 24 hours for a full charge. Every single challenge you do cost 1 and a lesson has about 10-15 challenges. Thats not even enough for a proper lesson per day anymore. You are no longer rewarded for getting the answers right, so you’re actually being punished for learning now which completely counterproductive to what they claim….  Theres a very simple fix to all this, leave the charge, remove the ads and allow us to watch ads to fully charge up again. Everyone wins that way but no they obviously chose greed and im not for it. I only gave it 2 stars because you can actually play chess without using charge, but i wonder how long they’ll leave it this way before finding a way to lock unlimited play behind their subscriptions.

I used this regularly to help improve my Spanish before visiting several Spanish speaking countries. I found the lessons to be very very repetitive. 

As an adult, I do not appreciate the games that you can’t get past unless you just do them. Some of the things are extremely simplistic. 

I canceled my subscription, but then something popped up. I may have accidentally hit a link that continued my subscription for an additional year!!! That’s really annoying. I have cancelled again. But in the meantime, I’ve had to pay a lot of money for something that I find extremely annoying at times and not very effective. 

I also don’t use Spain Spanish and it seems like that’s exactly what this uses! So I end up having mistakes when I didn’t make a mistake in my area.

Don’t get this app!!!!

title: Not dyslexic/disgraphic friendly on app
body:
The app punishes you by taking a heart away  (unlike online) which is Incredibly frustrating when you flip letters. I check and double check my typing but only occasionally get “oops” you have a typo. Usually it eats heart after heart in a discouraging spiral with only costly (in time or money) ways to gain an accommodation. Sometimes I have to log in online to be able to make my daily goal or repeat over and over mastered stuff to regain hearts to make forward progress.  

I watched the Ted talk about this program and got really excited about the crowed sourcing idea. I keep picking it up to try again and then put it down discouraged.   

If it didn’t do that I’d love the app.  

I’ve been consistently using this app for years a bit at a time failing a lot due to the spelling. But mostly making my each months 50 point goal to get a badge. If you fail they make it easier (annoying I noticed this year it reduced to 45 if I missed the previous badge)  but last month it jumped to 60 points to get the monthly badge! What no! Just managed to do that for August, but for September the goal post is now 65 points. I’m giving up why get the badge if I can miss September and it will drop down again. Trying for the badge feels like work instead of fun. Can I communicate with my Spanish clients sort of, so yeah but I struggle to form sentences. Would much rather learn to speak it than spell. But all the good speaking parts are the next tier up and for that price I can take a local Spanish speaking practice class. 

Put the monthly badges back to 50 points please.

title: Bring back the old app setup and lower the Energy cost!
body: Ever since I downloaded Duolingo on my iPad, it had an amazing glitch. The button always said "Start for 15 Energy," but it never actually subtracted anything from my battery! title: Endless frustration
body:
Duolingo's courses have declined tremendously in terms of quality. I am saying this as a user with a streak of over 3200 days.

I have started to experience daily frustration since a recent update, because now Duolingo keeps marking my alternative yet perfectly good translations as "wrong", only because I was not using the exact word that it wanted me to. Follow-up explanations were generally unhelpful, because they fail to convince me why my answers were "wrong"; instead they keep brainwashing me why only their answers were "okay". I don't see any reason why "在另一个星系中" is the only acceptable translation to "in another galaxy", while "在另一个星系" is seen as wrong. I keep sending feedbacks on how my answers should have been accepted, yet I have not received a single response since - years ago they would at least bother to let me know that they decided to accept my answer.

Language training should never teach learners to be overly paranoid about meaningless, menial details; it should teach learners how to express themselves with their limited knowledge of a second language. As a linguist myself I am very disappointed in Duolingo's courses nowadays. Make some changes before it's too late.

content.label:
Duolingo's courses have declined tremendously in terms of quality. I am saying this as a user with a streak of over 3200 days.

I have started to experience daily frustration since a recent update, because now Duolingo keeps marking my alternative yet perfectly good translations as "wrong", only because I was not using the exact word that it wanted me to. Follow-up explanations were generally unhelpful, because they fail to convince me why my answers were "wrong"; instead they keep brainwashing me why only their answers were "okay". I don't see any reason why "在另一个星系中" is the only acceptable translation to "in another galaxy", while "在另一个星系" is seen as wrong. I keep sending feedbacks on how my answers should have been accepted, yet I have not received a single response since - years ago they would at least bother to let me know that they decided to accept my answer.

Language training should never teach learners to be overly paranoid about meaningless, menial details; it should teach learners how to express themselves with their limited knowledge of a second language. As a linguist myself I am very disappointed in Duolingo's courses nowadays. Make some changes before it's too late.

title: Good but so annoying…
body:
Every lesson you are greeted with a money hungry ad that ask you to pay for super Duolingo also, I am unsure why you have a battery to do your Duolingo. I don’t like how I can run out of battery when I am on the edge of losing my streak also to mention the streak, the streak has been pretty annoying. I get a big screen on my face that I’m going to lose my 100+ streak. You should’ve just added a option where I can choose to pause my streak I’m trying to do important things and I don’t have too much time to fit in my Duolingo then not to mention after any lesson a corny little animation of Duolingo pops up some of them are not corny, but a lot of them are it’s genuinely so annoying a lot of things I would like to see improvement in is less money, hungry ads after every single session and at least give us the opportunity to pause our streaks when we might not be able to get to it yesterday, I was just chilling playing the game with my cousin and we both had our Duolingo we both got very disappointed because it just pops up at the wrong moments like I said the game is good in all but the stuff I mentioned is really getting on my nerves


Next time if I were to get an app to learn a new language it would be an app that doesn’t require corny animations money, hungry ads and definitely no streaks that you have to follow every single day


Oh, and the corny pictures were personal There is indeed kids on this app. Just thought I’d need to add that too 


        thanks for listening
